items.issue: The HJH source includes potassium; the previous app used the no-potassium variant.

items.issue: HJH page 54 prints the high-risk age factor as 'Age > 65'. The validated Canadian C-Spine Rule (Stiell et al., JAMA 2001) uses 'Age >= 65 years', so a patient of exactly 65 must be treated as high-risk rather than excluded.
items.decision: Two-person clinical review authorised applying the validated 'Age >= 65 years' threshold.
items.applicationAction: The canonical entry still mirrors the immutable supplied source ('Age > 65'); the validated 'Age >= 65 years' value is applied to the effective runtime record via the reviewed score-corrections overlay (src/clinical/scoreCorrections.ts), preserving the source-mirror invariant.

items.topic: Hypokalaemia entry contaminated with hypernatraemia content
items.issue: The category-browse hypokalaemia entry cited page 95 but its clinical_features and all ten management_steps were a verbatim copy of the page 96 HYPERNATRAEMIA payload - including 'Aim to correct Na+ by 10-12mmol/l in 24hrs', 'Causes of Hypernatraemia' and DDAVP/diabetes-insipidus text. Only its drugs list held genuine potassium content, truncated mid-word. A clinician opening Hypokalaemia was shown sodium-correction instructions. This is a further instance of the documented HJH extraction root cause (fixed-size text windows from adjacent pages attached to correctly titled records); the same topic already rendered correctly on the HJH protocol-library page, which consumes clinical-sources/corrections/HJH/hypokalaemia.json.
items.decision: Two-person clinical review approved replacing the contaminated payload with the page-95 content already reviewed against the PDF (review_state 'reviewed-against-pdf-page-95').
items.applicationAction: Entry rebuilt from the verified page-95 source text (K+ < 3.5 mmol/l; simultaneous K and Mg replacement; 40 mmol KCl + 2g MgSO4 in 200 ml 0.9% NaCl over 4 hours via pump/dial-a-flow at 50 ml/hr; life-threatening arrest dose 20 mEq/mmol KCl (10 ml) at 1 ml/min then re-check). Both rendering paths now agree; a regression test asserts the entry contains no sodium-correction text.
